name: 2021 S. Prairie Avenue — the alley building of the house at 2021 (district draft; refined by T-1938)

function.note: The 1911 sheet reads '2-storey brick building on the alley lettered GARAGE, its upper storey tin-clad, with a one-storey south end'. 1911 labels it a garage or barn; for 1904 the envelope is backcast and its use reconstructed as a stable/coach house.

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2352, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1938 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 35 trace (s35fp-2021-b2), the T-1842 census (s35-2021-rear) and the T-1837 register row frontage-35-079; every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-prairie-20-22-east-2352).

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

position.symbolic_location: 2021 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_2021 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).
position.note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 0.500, v -6.000 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, a similarity on two degrees of freedom that says little away from them, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of trace on this coarser copy. Rotation 179.389 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle that fits inside the traced main part (u toward the street, v along the front). The building's other rectangles are in draft_plan.

stories.note: The census reading '2-storey brick building on the alley lettered GARAGE, its upper storey tin-clad, with a one-storey south end': 2 storeys.

construction.note: The trace's fabric colour on the main part: brick.

parts.from: s35fp-2021-b2 outline (main, brick), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 76% of its fill

draft_plan.note: Rectangles fitted inside the traced parts by the rules' fit (cell 0.25 m, at most 3 a part, to 90% cover): s35fp-2021-b2 outline (main, brick), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 76% of its fill. Roles: the main part's largest rectangle is the main body; a shallow rectangle at the front is a bay; the sheet's ranges, porches and stone fronts keep their roles. Storeys per piece and roof per piece are the draft rules' (reconstructed).

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row 'service' overlaid with the frontage row: The James L. High house (built for Benjamin Adams in the late 1870s; High's from 1886, with his 1887 rear range): the register's 'steep main gable, conical rounded corner tower, arched entry' as a steep gable to the avenue over the 2½B body and a round tower under a cone on the north front corner, where the sheet draws its front projection. Its broad side wing's secondary gable is T-1917's. Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 1698949506 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %. Liberty L-draft-prairie-20-22-east-2352.
